```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Problem 1

```{r load-penguins}
data("penguins", package = "palmerpenguins")
```

The penguins dataset contains measurements of adult penguins near Palmer Station in Antarctica. It has `r nrow(penguins)` rows and `r ncol(penguins)` columns.

The species are `r paste(levels(penguins$species), collapse = ", ")`. The islands are `r paste(levels(penguins$island), collapse = ", ")`. Other variables include bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, sex, and year. Bill and flipper measurements are in millimeters, and body mass is in grams. Sex includes female and male, with some missing values. The study years range from `r min(penguins$year)` to `r max(penguins$year)`.

The mean flipper length is `r round(mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 2)` mm. Missing values are excluded from this calculation.

```{r penguin-plot}
penguin_plot = ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(
    x = bill_length_mm,
    y = flipper_length_mm,
    color = species
  )
) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Bill length (mm)",
    y = "Flipper length (mm)",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

penguin_plot

ggsave(
  filename = "penguin_scatterplot.png",
  plot = penguin_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```

Species is a categorical variable, so the plot uses a separate color for each species. Rows missing either plotted measurement are omitted.
